item.title: Contributions of connected devices and telemonitoring in home dialysis
item.description: Home dialysis, including peritoneal dialysis and home hemodialysis, is a treatment option for patients with end-stage renal disease that offers greater independence and improved quality of life. However, its widespread use remains limited by safety concerns, technical complexity, and challenges with remote clinical monitoring.In this context, the development of connected devices and telemonitoring represents a significant advance. item.title: Use of high doses of intraperitoneal amikacin to preserve the peritoneal catheter during pseudomonas peritonitis
item.description: This article reports a clinical case illustrating the use of high-dose intraperitoneal amikacin to preserve the peritoneal catheter in a patient with Pseudomonas aeruginosa peritonitis undergoing chronic peritoneal dialysis. item.title: Trends in Assisted Peritoneal Dialysis in France Over 45 Years: Data from the RDPLF Registry
item.description: BackgroundAssisted peritoneal dialysis (PD) has played an important role in France by enabling elderly and frail patients to access home dialysis despite limited autonomy, supported by the widespread involvement of home nursing care. The aim of this study is to describe the evolution of assisted PD in France using data from the RDPLF registry.MethodsIncident PD patients recorded between 1981 and 2025 were analyzed and grouped into consecutive 5-year periods.
